items.prompt: Your friend is talking to you. What shows you are listening?
hints: Good listeners use their eyes and ears.
Think about what your body does.
What could you do with your head to show you understand?
items.explanation: Looking at the speaker and nodding shows you are listening.

options.text: Look at your friend and nod.
Look away and hum a song.
options.why: This shows you are not listening.
Wait for your turn to talk.
Your friend will think you do not care.

items.prompt: Read the text aloud. Read clearly and not too fast.
hints: Read it once in your head first.
Take a breath at each full stop.
items.explanation: Pausing at each full stop helps the listener follow.
items.readText: Sam has a big black dog. The dog likes to run and dig. Sam and his dog play in the park every day.

items.prompt: You want to join a game. What do you say?
hints: Ask in a kind way.
Use the magic word.
Which one is a polite question?
items.explanation: Can I play with you, please? is a kind and polite way to ask.

options.why: This is bossy. Ask kindly.

options.text: Can I play with you, please?

options.why: This is unkind.
This is unkind.

items.prompt: Read this aloud. Make your voice go up for the question. Sound excited for the shout.
hints: Find the question mark and the exclamation marks first.
Practise the question in a curious voice.
items.explanation: A question mark tells you to let your voice go up. An exclamation mark tells you to read with a big feeling.

criteria.label: Voice goes up for the question

items.readText: 'Where is my hat?' asked Pak Tono. He looked under the bed. He looked behind the door. 'Here it is!' shouted his little girl. It was on his head!

items.prompt: You did not hear what your teacher said. What is the polite thing to say?
hints: Be polite to your teacher.
Use sorry and please.
Which one asks kindly?
items.explanation: Sorry, could you say that again, please? is polite and helps you find out.

options.why: This sounds rude.
This is bossy.

options.text: Sorry, could you say that again, please?

options.why: Then you will not know what to do.

items.prompt: Describe your favourite animal. Say what it looks like, where it lives and what it eats.
hints: Start with: My favourite animal is.
Use describing words, like stripy or fluffy.
items.explanation: Give the listener details: how it looks, where it lives and what it eats.

items.prompt: Which question would help you find out more about your friend's holiday?
hints: The question should be about the holiday.
Good questions get a long answer.
Which question starts with what and asks about the holiday?
items.explanation: What was the best part of your holiday? is about the holiday and gets your friend talking.

options.why: This is not about the holiday.
This is not about the holiday.
This is not about the holiday.

options.text: What was the best part of your holiday?

items.prompt: Think of a story you read this week. Retell it in your own words. Tell the beginning, the middle and the end.
hints: Say who is in the story first.
Use first, then and in the end.
items.explanation: A good retelling keeps the events in order and names the characters.

criteria.label: Tells the beginning, middle and end
Uses time words, like first, then and in the end

items.prompt: Your group is talking about a book. What is good group talk?
hints: Everyone should get a turn.
Think about how the others feel.
What helps a group work well?
items.explanation: In good group talk, everyone takes turns and listens to each other.

options.text: Take turns and listen to others.

options.why: Others need a turn too.
Shouting makes it hard for everyone.

options.text: Only talk to your best friend.
options.why: Talk to the whole group.

items.prompt: Tell someone how to make a sandwich. Give the steps in order.
hints: Think about what you need first.
Say first, next, then and finally.
items.explanation: Spoken instructions need the same things as written ones: steps in order and time words.

criteria.label: Uses first, next, then and finally

items.prompt: A character in a story whispers a secret. How should you read that part aloud?
hints: Think about what whispering sounds like.
Your voice should match the character.
Is a secret loud or quiet?
items.explanation: A whisper is quiet, so a quiet, soft voice fits a secret.

options.why: Shouting does not fit a secret.
This does not fit a whisper.
Singing does not fit a whisper.

items.prompt: Read the poem aloud. Keep a steady beat and make the rhymes clear.
hints: Clap the beat before you read.
Make the rhyming words clear: blue, too, run, sun.
items.explanation: A steady beat and clear rhymes help the listener enjoy a poem.
items.readText:
My kite is red and green and blue,
it has a long tail, yellow too.
I hold the string and run, run, run
across the field beneath the sun.

items.prompt: Choose the best reply. 'How are you today?'
hints: The question asks how you feel.
It is polite to ask back.
Find the answer about feeling.
items.explanation: The question asks how you feel. The best reply answers it and politely asks back.

options.why: This answers: How old are you?
This answers a question that starts with do.
This answers: What is it?

options.text: I'm fine, thank you. And you?

items.prompt: You are telling the class about your weekend. What should you do?
hints: Think about your voice.
Think about your eyes.
What helps everyone hear and enjoy your talk?
items.explanation: Speaking clearly and looking at the class helps everyone listen.

options.text: Speak very fast and look at the floor.
options.why: The class will not hear or see you well.

options.text: Whisper so no one can hear.
options.why: Everyone needs to hear you.

options.text: Speak clearly and look at your audience.
Read a book about someone else.
options.why: Talk about your own weekend.

items.prompt: Which is better, a rainy day or a sunny day? Say what you think. Give two reasons and use because.
hints: Start with: I think ... is better.
Then say: because ... and because ...
items.explanation: A good opinion says what you think and gives reasons with because.

items.prompt: Choose the best reply. 'Would you like some more rice?'
hints: The question offers you something.
We answer with please or thank you.
Which reply says no politely?
items.explanation: No, thank you. I'm full. is a polite way to say no to more food.

options.why: Would you like needs yes, please or no, thank you.
This does not answer the question.
This does not answer the question.

items.prompt: Pretend you are a guide at a market. Tell visitors what they can see, buy, smell and taste.
hints: Picture a busy market first.
Talk to your visitors: Look! Smell this!
Use describing words for colours and smells.
items.explanation: A good guide speaks to the listeners and uses the senses to bring a place to life.

criteria.label: Talks about at least three senses
Speaks to the audience, like 'Look over here!'
